READ-ONLY SCOPE CORRECTION on bd-01M168TZ3VRQYSE7TNT5JKJTSJ; no claim or edit.

The recorded blocking condition says this must close before any artifact renders OR EXPORTS recall text. That boundary is already present on current main 451221b:

- codec/recall.scala gives a public Encoder[RecallGraph[Checked]] and inserts g.transcript.
- codec/core.scala encodes StorySource.rawText and StorySource.canonicalText.
- StoryModelCodecSuite exercises Canonical.encode(recall) and exact round trip.
- The encoder Scaladoc is stale: it says plain StorySource is temporary until the ADR 0001 PseudonymizedText/ReidentificationKey split lands, but that split is already implemented.

CHAIN: permits YES; repository non-test occurrence NOT FOUND; produces YES, full transcript JSON by construction; external consumption UNKNOWN. This does not by itself prove a live leak, so I am not promoting priority, but it invalidates the premise that only a future renderer creates the export seam. The existing generic encoder cannot distinguish raw participant text from certified pseudonymized text because RecallSegmenter accepts StorySource and RecallGraph carries no witness.

Acceptance should therefore cover the codec now, not only the future split-screen:
1. a raw RecallGraph cannot enter a public/export-safe encoding path merely because metadata says pseudonymized;
2. the proof-bearing path binds the exact graph transcript and atlas source to the exact PseudonymizedTranscript payload;
3. a mismatched witness fails;
4. any encoded certified artifact omits ReidentificationKey and original surfaces;
5. decoding must be contextual or encoder-only unless it can re-establish certification, matching ADR 0001 D6, which already says a future codec cannot reconstruct omitted source text to rerun PseudonymizedText.checked.

Dependency constraint: recall cannot carry interview.PseudonymizedTranscript because interview depends on recall; recall also does not depend on embed-core. The likely ownership seam is an interview-owned unforgeable graph-plus-transcript wrapper consumed by codec, or an explicit export authority passed to codec. A boolean, metadata string, or caller-asserted Sensitivity repeats the rejected ungrounded-license defect. Removing or gating the existing generic encoder is source/API compatibility work and needs chief/ADR disposition.
